test_title: PYST 86: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 05 Mar, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom

Go down like a lead balloon

options.text: Put yourself in a tough position in order to support someone / something
To be received badly by an audience

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 4**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The idiom **"Go down like a lead balloon"** means to be received badly by an audience. (दर्शकों द्वारा बुरी तरह से स्वीकार किया जाना) • **Example:** His joke during the presentation **went down like a lead balloon.** • **To be received badly by an audience** refers to a situation where something, such as a performance or a joke, fails to impress or entertain the audience. (दर्शकों द्वारा बुरी तरह से स्वीकार किया जाना) • **Example:** The new product launch** went down like a lead balloon** with the customers. Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Put yourself in a tough position in order to support someone / something** (किसी का / किसी चीज़ का समर्थन करने के लिए अपने आप को कठिन स्थिति में डालना): • **Example:** He put himself in a tough position to support his friend during the crisis. • **Surrender** (आत्मसमर्पण करना): • **Example:** The soldiers had to surrender after running out of ammunition. • **To gamble everything you have** (जो कुछ भी आपके पास है, उस पर जुआ खेलना): • **Example:** He decided to gamble everything he had on that risky investment. 37:Tc4e, The correct answer is **Option 2**.
